Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the candid conversation last week. Per our note on the call, I ran a short audit of Brightline's last 90 days of token consumption and performance characteristics and attached the Q3 usage audit and the raw ledger. High level: you're running heavier inference on long-context summarization flows (avg seq ~1,800 tokens) and a bursty nightly batch that is pushing headroom in our current tranche. That pattern is what caused the surprise earlier this month.

Next steps I propose:
- Quick triage call to confirm the two burst windows and whether you want a straight tranche uplift vs. staged commit (30/60/10).
- If you want a staged uplift, we can provide a short pilot (30% extra tranche) for one month and measure prefix-KV cache hit improvement and unit-cost delta.
- I attached a redline SOW for the tranche upgrade so legal can move quickly if you decide to proceed.

I've looped Karthik for pricing scenarios and Ben for the operational impact on Dedicated pools. Available windows for a 30-minute sync: tomorrow 10–11am PT or Wednesday 1–2pm PT.

Thanks,

Alex — quick note on the modeling requests you made. I pulled a few scenarios off the ledger: baseline (no change), staged uplift 30% for 30 days, and full tranche uplift (equivalent to +80% committed capacity). Key bullets below — full calc in the Drive link I shared in the thread.

- Baseline: projected overage risk in Q4 if nightly batch continues; unit price remains same but burst costs (on-demand) could add ~18–22% to monthly spend in highest week.
- 30% staged uplift (30 days): modeled net spend delta +9–11% versus baseline, but expected to eliminate on-demand bursts in 85% of observed nights; unit cost effectively improves by 6% due to better sustained batching and prefix cache hit.
- Full tranche uplift (+80%): upfront commit increases committed spend ~62% but reduces on-demand exposure; unit cost improvement ~15% and latency SLOs easier to hit for 2k-token runs.

On burst credits: we can offer a one-time pilot concession (equivalent to two nights of burst credits) if Brightline runs the 30% staged uplift pilot and we observe a >=50% reduction in nightly peak demand due to scheduling adjustments and caching. We'll formalize in SOW.

Latency SLOs: for long-context jobs we're targeting p95 <= 850ms on our L4 profile for a 2k-token step (depends on model selection). Ben can confirm operational constraints.

Happy to walk through numbers Wed at 1pm PT.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
